children: Indian benchmark indices extended their losing streak for the second consecutive session on September 8, with the Nifty hitting a nearly three-month low amid selling pressure in IT, oil & gas and banking stocks.

After a weak opening, the market staged a brief pullback in the initial hours but failed to sustain gains as profit booking intensified. The Nifty touched a day’s low of 23,623.10 before recovering marginally and closing at 23,635 after the Closing Auction Session (CAS).
At close, the Sensex was down 555.23 points or 0.73 percent at 75,577.58, and the Nifty was down 144.05 points or 0.61 percent at 23,635.10.
The broader market outperformed the main indices with Nifty midcap and smallcap indices ended marginally higher.
Top Nifty losers were ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, SBI Life Insurance, L&T, UltraTech Cement, while gainers included Bharat Electronics, ONGC, HUL, Eicher Motors and Adani Ports.
Among sectors, Private Bank index shed 1%, Oil & Gas index down 0.67%, Nifty Bank down 0.5% and IT index shed 0.37%, while Media index added 1.3%, Pharma index rose 0.7% and FMCG index gained 0.35%.
More than 200 stocks touched 52-week high including TVS Holdings, Solar Industries, Piramal Pharma, Divis Labs, among others. Click to View More

On the other hand more than 100 stocks touched 52-week low, including Voltas, United Breweries, ICICI Lombard, Indiamart Intermesh, JK Lakshmi Cement, IRCTC, Cello World, Dabur India, P&G Hygiene, Godrej Consumer, , among others. Click to View More

Among individual stocks, Novartis India share price rose 11% after it entered into an exclusive promotion and distribution agreement with Novartis Healthcare. Hindustan Aeronautics gained 3.5% after CLSA maintained an ‘outperform’ rating with a target price of Rs 5,481. GE Vernova T&D surged 9% after emerging as the L1 bidder for a 6,000 MW, ±800 kV HVDC LCC terminal station for renewable power evacuation from Barmer II to South Kalamb.

Sansera Engineering rose more than 3% to hit a 52-week high after CLSA initiated coverage with an ‘outperform’ rating and target price of Rs 4,954. Deep Industries advanced 4% on securing an Rs 88.15 crore contract from ONGC.

Behari Lal Engineering fell 5% despite reporting a 24.5% jump in Q1 profit to Rs 19.2 crore and Neuland Laboratories gained 4% after its board approved Rs 126 crore capex for the purchase of around 134 acres of land at Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh.

After witnessing flat closes in the previous two sessions, the Indian rupee came under pressure on September 8, falling 33 paise to close at 94.82 per dollar, compared with the previous close of 94.49.
New Listings
Deepa Jewellers shares ended 10% higher at Rs 194.7 after making a strong debut at Rs 221 on the NSE, a 24.86% premium to its IPO issue price of Rs 177 per share.
Rays of Belief shares ended 4% lower at Rs 228.75 after making a flat debut on the stock exchanges at Rs 239 apiece.
Outlook for September 9
Rupak De, Senior Technical Analyst at LKP Securities
The index has slipped again as rising crude oil prices are expected to put inflationary pressure. The Nifty has found initial support near the previous swing low.
In addition, on the daily timeframe, the RSI is showing a positive divergence, suggesting a potential shift in momentum.

Going forward, 23,600 is likely to act as a crucial support for the Nifty. If the index holds above 23,600, we may see a decent recovery, which could take the Nifty towards 24,000 and higher in the short term.
Shrikant Chouhan, Head Equity Research, Kotak Securities

Today, the benchmark indices continued profit booking at higher levels. The Nifty ends 144 points lower, while the Sensex was down by 555 points. Among sectors, the Defense index outperformed, rallying 2.52 percent, whereas the Private Bank and Financial indices shed nearly 1 percent. Technically, after a gap-down open, the market has been consistently facing selling pressure at higher levels. On daily charts, the market has formed a bearish candle, and on intraday charts, it is holding a lower top formation, which is largely negative.

For day traders, 23750/75800 would act as an immediate resistance zone. Below this, a weak formation is likely to continue. On the downside, the market could retest the levels of 23500-23450/75200-75000. On the flip side, if the index closes above 23750/75800, the pullback could extend till 23850-23900/76000-76300.
